title: feat | Vertical branches in Git Diagram
body:
A new feature that helps create Vertical branches for GitDiagram.
Resolves #2585
Issue #4451 closed as a duplicate, please refer to #2585
Discussed #3772
author: mastersibin

comments.author: nirname
comments.body: We need some tests covering that feature

comments.author: mastersibin
comments.body: I am not familiar with testing. Can you please guide me on how to do it?

comments.author: nirname
comments.body: There are 2 kinds of tests for the project. Unit tests (vitest) and integration tests or end-2-end tests (cypress). Unit tests check if a function works as expected, integration tests check what a user sees in browser. Please, skim through [testing section of contributing guidelines](https://mermaid.js.org/community/development.html#unit-tests), and feel free to ask if you have any questions.

comments.author: mastersibin
comments.body:
In the documentation, it's mentioned, we don't have to unit test renderers. 
https://mermaid.js.org/community/development.html#unit-tests:~:text=Unit%20tests%20are%20mandatory%20all%20code%20except%20the%20renderers.%20(The%20renderers%20are%20tested%20with%20integration%20tests.)

comments.author: nirname
comments.body: We use cypress for testing rendering

comments.author: mastersibin
comments.body: I have added tests in cypress. Did all the tests which were done on horizontal branches.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Explicitly requests adding tests to cover the new feature, which is a concrete code change.

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
You haven't really applied direction. Take a look at `flow` and `class` diagram and see how they implement direction.

`git` graph should only have two directions for now, `LR` and `TB`.

comments.author: mastersibin
comments.body:
They use graphlib and set the direction. I think we can't use graphlib for gitgraph because we don't have vertices and edges and we form gitgraphs with a different logic.

Do we have to create something like graphlib for gitgraphs?

comments.author: mastersibin
comments.body: As discussed, I didn't change anything in the grammar, except removing BT and adding TB.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Points out that direction has not been properly implemented, references other diagrams as examples to follow, and specifies that only LR and TB directions should be supported — all implying concrete code changes.
